newsitem.title: USA: Minnesota proposes to remove gang tattoos.
newsitem.headline: Minnesota proposes to remove gang tattoos.

text.p: Gang members' tattoos would be removed at their request at state expense under a proposal from a Minnesota lawmaker who said Friday the markings can be an impediment to those wanting to leave the gang life.
"Nobody is going to hire someone who has 'Killer' tattooed on his forehead," said State Representative Wes Skoglund, who sponsored the legislation, which sets aside $500,000 for the programme.
Taxpayer funds would only pay for removal of tattoos "on the person's face, neck, hands, or arms that identifies the person as being affiliated with a criminal gang," the proposal said.
The gang member would have to be younger than 25 and deemed employable. Former gang members may be required to perform community service to repay the cost.
